reviews.text:

Thought it was some kind of country restrictions but tried outlook and that worked first time so gave up and uninstalled it and now sticking permanently with outlook. I was also getting 20 or 30 spam emails per day using this app from same blocked senders using randomised email addresses but since moving to outlook I’m getting none which is in itself suspicious 🤔

Developers response does not clear this up at all and hence my truthful review remains. 20 or 30 spam a day using this app. 0 to 2 per day, when using Outlook. Fact. Sticking with Outlook thank you.

reviews.title: **Furious**
reviews.text:
Just had the same experience as the February 2026 user. I've been using Edison Mail mobile and desktop apps for the last four or five years, and suddenly I can no longer access my desktop app. There's only a notification window -- with no Close button, so it can't be closed -- with an asinine smiley face and text that says Edison is switching to mobile-only immediately, Edison is removing the desktop app from the App Store, and Edison won't respond to any requests for support. The window can't even be expanded in order to see all of the text, which is insane. 

There is text that says “You can keep using it if you’d like, but starting now…”. But that statement isn’t true — and is basically total BS — since the window can’t be closed and there’s an error message in the background that says something about “wound”. This is an example of (bad) marketing language trying to provide a cover for horrible engineering, product, and ‘leadership’ decisions. AI, anyone?

They gave ZERO advance notification about this. All of this is a complete violation of industry standards, but I guess who cares because standards don't exist any more, right?

Now I need to figure out the implications of a company choosing to do whatever it wants with all of my personal email, as they've chosen to do with this desktop app. Given this and the security issues they've had over the years -- and I thought I had done enough research -- you can be absolutely sure they're doing some back-door thing where they'v

reviews.title: Shocking privacy violations!
reviews.text: I was testing this app for a family member and added my own account to experiment with. There were a couple of things that made it unsuitable and so I removed it shortly afterwards. Much to my surprise I noticed in the mail server logs (I run my own server) that something was still downloading my entire mailbox… The IP address belonged to AWS and I have since discovered that Edison use AWS for their services, save your configuration details (including username and password) and continue using them to download your mail even if you uninstall the app! No doubt this is buried away in their Terms & Conditions but this is something they should surely be shouting about up front as I absolutely would not have consented had I known. I feel really quite angry about this.
